    "body": "## Why\n\nInstaller ownership checks could claim user commands containing `codecortex`, delete neighboring user hooks, or report malformed configuration removal as success. The first archive publisher could overwrite a pointer created by another writer after its initial check. Unchanged index scans also retained an owned action entry for every unchanged file.\n\n## Changes\n\n- Match Claude Code hooks by exact owned command and event shape, preserve neighboring commands, and validate configuration before changing other files.\n- Reject malformed generic JSON installer sections and preserve bytes when uninstall has nothing to remove.\n- Publish an initially absent archive `latest` pointer with create-if-absent semantics; retain existing-owned pointer update behavior.\n- Keep only add/update/dirty-resolution actions in the scan action map, with scanned-path membership representing unchanged files. Existing scan, hashing, resolver, resource, and admission budgets remain in force.\n\nThe product commit changes exactly eight Rust source/test files and two Python validation files. A separate independent source review inventories all 1,096 product inputs and 142 validation inputs. The final admission commit changes only the four v15 source/review pins and its registry. Existing approval algorithms, historical snapshots, CI selection, and source exclusions remain unchanged.\n\n## Validation and limits\n\nFocused regressions passed on their recorded reviewed sources, including 56 installer unit tests, five installer CLI tests, 42 archive-publication tests, and 36 distinct index planning/reconciliation tests. Independent reviewers additionally checked ownership, failure preservation, first-publication races, and dense/sparse action equivalence. These executions retain their original source identities; identical product bytes are not described as a new execution on this PR head.\n\nPrior integration validation passed formatting, workspace clippy, compilation of default targets, 421 P8 Python tests, the completed remaining Rust targets, and the named fixture/corpus test. Two unchanged default runtime tests failed in the local execution environment and are not waived. The complete historical source proof is also locally blocked by two unavailable original binary Git inputs. Ordinary GitHub CI on the final PR head is required before merge.\n\nNo full-build performance improvement, full-scale acceptance, original TODO completion, or release certification is claimed. The sparse-action measurements concern only that component.\n\n## Original TODO accounting\n\nThe original ledger remains 192 total: 163 done, 16 in progress, 12 todo, and one blocked; 29 remain. This PR contributes four scoped fixes and claims zero newly completed original TODOs. P8-005 full-scale evidence still gates the next original acceptance sequence. No existing expensive study is duplicated or dispatched by this PR workflow.\n\n## Review structure\n\n- Product: `306c53bf600fcd0614bbb50d7409acfce69c3972`\n- Independent review: `5f911c78af7d305476ad83286d602ee6c19b7aa5`\n- Admission: `065f5ab5da1bc5de74cbd3e4c360b51e09200687`\n- The independent review record contains public repository identities, file hashes, and scope limits. Raw local execution logs, host metadata, environment details, and Git bundles are excluded from this PR.\n",
